say: Someone bought google dot com. For twelve dollars.

text: September 2015. A former Google employee was searching Google's own domain shop.
say: September twenty fifteen. A former Google employee was searching Google's own domain shop.

text: He typed in google.com. It said: available. $12.
say: He typed in google dot com. It said: available. Twelve dollars.

text: So he bought it. For about one minute, he owned the most visited website on Earth.
Then an email arrived. Order cancelled.
Google paid him a reward: $6,006.13. Squint, and the number spells Google.
say: Google paid him a reward: six thousand and six dollars, thirteen cents. Squint, and the number spells Google.

text: He gave it to charity, so Google doubled it.
And Google isn't the only giant to lose its own domain.
In 1999, Microsoft forgot to renew passport.com, and Hotmail broke for many users.
say: In nineteen ninety-nine, Microsoft forgot to renew passport dot com, and Hotmail broke for many users.

text: A programmer paid the $35 renewal fee for them.
say: A programmer paid the thirty-five dollar renewal fee for them.

text: The lesson: if your domain expires, your website and your email go with it.
